tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Gerhard Albersheim in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: 1. X. Mozart Nachtmusik; Eroica begonnen.

8. Facsimile-Buch Mikulitsch gezeigt;Karl Lothar Mikulicz, Ein Notierungsbuch von Beethoven aus dem Besitze der Preussischen Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin (Leipzig: Breitkopf & Härtel, 1927): a transcription of “Landsberg 7,” which contains sketches primarily for The Creatures of Prometheus, Op. 43, and the sonatas Op. 23, 24, and 26. aus Beethoven op. 10III Menuett: Tauschstelle.

10. Aus Nottebohms SkizzenbuchGustav Nottebohm, Ein Skizzenbuch von Beethoven aus dem Jahre 1803 (Leipzig: Breitkopf & Härtel, 1880), with selective transcriptions from, and commentary on, “Landsberg 6,” commonly known as the “Eroica” Sketchbook. Skizzen zum 1. Satz, wie sie zu lesen sind.
19. 1. Satz, Bildkorrektur beendet.
22. Nachträgliche Erläuterungen; Eintragungen aus der rev. Abschr.; Vortrag im Großen.

26. Sommernachtstraum Ouvertüre:Diary Oct 23: “I work on the Overture to A Midsummer Night's Dream for Albersheim.” – An undated sketch for a graph of this work is preserved as part of OC 48/13. Bild der Urlinie, Entschleierung der letzten Geheimnisse der Parallelismen. A. bezeichnet den Besuch der Nilius-KurseRudolf Nilius (1883–1962), Austrian conductor and composer; diary Oct 26: “Albersheim already complains after the first lesson that Nilius is a waste of time for him.” – Diary Oct 15: “From 8:30 to 11, concert of the Philharmonic under Nilius ([broadcast] to the central European region): [...] – a refreshing evening, the tempos mainly correct, in spite of certain liberties taken in the dances.” The program was titled “Music from Austria” and included works by Haydn, Mozart, Schubert, and Johann Strauss the Elder and the Younger. als Zeitverlust.
29. 2. Satz der Eroica begonnen.

5. XI. Wieder Durchsicht des 1. Satzes begonnen, Erläuterung einiger Stellen dazu.Diary Nov 5: “Albersheim attempts to make hasty progress on the symphony – not out of craving, more out of curiosity; I succeed in curbing this and summon him back to his obligation to precision.”

9. Marsch aus der Sommernachtstraum-Musik, Bild der Urlinie u. Vortrag.Diary Nov 7: “From Albersheim (postcard): he asks for the Wedding March by Mendelssohn, to be explained as early as midday; I write it out after lunch.”
Bemerkungen zu Hoesslins Vortrag von Brahms I. Sinfonie zu Berlioz Symphonie phantastique; Scherzo begonnen.
16. Bild des 4. Satzes. Fragen zu Schuberts Sinfonie Bdur.
26. Fragen zu Schuberts Rosamunde Ballett, Bd u. Gm-Stellen; zeige Hecks Skizzen zu Beethovens VI., letzter Satz.
30. Linie zu Schubert Cdur-Sinfonie, Andante, Fdur-Stelle; Linie zu Chopin Nocturne Fdur korrigirt; Linie Bach Toccata Fdur korrigirt.

3. XII. Mendelssohn „Die Liebende schreibt,“ Linie korrigirt;Diary Dec 1: “Work on Bach's Toccata and Mendelssohn's "Die Liebende schreibt" (for Albersheim).” -- The minuet, which is part of Schubert’s Piano Sonata in G major, D. 894, served as the principal case study in Schenker’s article Eine Rettung der klassischen Musik-Texte, Der Kunstwart vol. 42, No. 6 (March 1929). allerhand Beispiele zum Vortrag: Mozart Rondo Am, Schubert Sonate Bd; zeige den Abstand vom Facsimile u. Peters-Ausgabe im Menuett Hm von Schubert.
7. Bild-Korrektur des Finale abgeschlossen, zurück zum Scherzo.

17. Zeige Dunns Ornamentik,Petrie Dunn, Ornamentation in the Works of Chopin (London: Novello, 1921). den Sonderabdruck von Souchay;Marc-Andre Souchay, Das Thema in der Fuge Bachs (Leipzig: Breitkopf & Härtel, 1928); reprinted from the 1927 Bach-Jahrbuch. Chopin Etude op. 10III, Linie korrigirt.

21. Eintragungen
aus der rev. Abschrift, 2., 3., 4. Satz abgeschlossen; empfehle den Aufsatz von Landshoff in der „Musik“ u. das Selbst-Interview von Schönberg in der D.A.Z..Arnold Schoenberg, Interview mit mir selbst, Deutsche Allgemeine Zeitung, December 16, 1928. -- Diary Nov 14: “An issue of Die Musik purchased, containing an article by Landshoff and one on Brahms's Violin Concerto.” Ludwig Landshoff, Die Aufführungspraxis Bachscher Chorwerke, Die Musik, xxi/2 (November 1928), 81–97
24. XII.(!!) Vortrag des 2. u. 3. Satzes der Sinfonie.

31. Vortrag des Finale; Anmerkungen zum Vortrag von Beethovens II. Sinfonie (gegen Spörr 30. XII).On December 30, Austrian Radio (RAVAG) broadcast a concert given by the Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra under Martin Spörr, which concluded with a performance of Beethoven’s Second Symphony.

4. I. Auf die Ornamentik bezügliche Fragen aus Haydn-Sonaten, namentlich über den Doppelschlag von unten; über den Widerspruch in der Notierung von in Schubert Sinfonie Bd, 1. Satz; Haydn Sinfonie Ddur begonnen.Schenker’s diary (Dec 22) indicates that the Haydn symphony project had already been agreed some time before: “I work on Haydn Symphony in D major (Albersheim).” – Undated sketches of graphs for the symphony are preserved as OC 35/283 and 38/162 (first movement), and 35/302 (second movement).

7. Chopin Etude op. 10XII, Facsimile gezeigt; zum Vortrag von Beethoven Klavier-Konzert Cdur (Wang).Diary Jan 6, 1929: “Radio, 11 o'clock (Konrad): Brahms, Academic Festival Overture; Beethoven, Piano Concerto (Wang); Bruckner's Fourth.” – Stella Wang (1895–1974), Austrian pianist, for a time a pupil of Schenker’s friend Moriz Violin.
11. Winke zu Brahms Klavier-Violin-Sonate op. 78; für eine Geburtstagfeier in Köln.
21. Ich spiele Händel Suite No 2, 1. Satz, aus op. 13 von Beethoven das Adagio usw.
25. I. Haydn Abschluß des 1. Satzes, Vortrag.

28. Pedalstudien; bespreche Vrieslanders Korrektur zu Chopin Etude; Ornamentik in Haydn Sonate Edur bei Moscheles u. Päsler.Diary Jan 3, 1929: “Work on correcting the Schubert essay. — Haydn-Päsler arrives.” – This probably refers to Karl Päsler’s three-volume edition of Haydn’s keyboard sonatas, published by Breitkopf & Härtel c. 1918. Ignaz Moscheles prepared editions of eighteen sonatas, published around 1850 in Stuttgart by Eduard Hallberger and including Hob. XVI:31 in E major. — Diary Jan 28: “Albersheim inquires about my library, and about the publisher.”
1. II. Haydn: das Bild des Andante.Diary Jan 27: “after dinner, I work on the symphony by Haydn (for Albersheim).”
4. Haydn: das Bild des Menuetts.

8. Zeige Hobokens Marsch u. Brünauers Klavierstück.Diary Feb 1: “Hoboken brings his march and two earlier compositions.” – Jan 29, 1929: “I show [Hoboken] Brünauer's composition; he replies: ‘I too have a march, for piano four hands.’" – Diary Feb 6: “Correction of Hoboken's and Brünauer's compositions.”
11. Haydn: Finale; nimmt Urlaub bis 1. März.Diary Feb 10: “In the evening, I work on Haydn (for Albersheim).” — Diary Feb 11: “Haydn for Albersheim finished – he is travelling to the Paznaun Valley!”
4. III. Haydn abgeschlossen, einschließlich des Vortrags.Diary Feb 24: “8:30 to 10:45 and 2 to 3:15, fair copy of Haydn's Finale (for Albersheim).”

8. Mozart Sinfonie Esdur begonnen.Diary Feb 12: “Rush to complete the first movement; Lie-Liechen following me with the fair copy on account of the necessity of making a start on Mozart's Symphony in E while Albersheim is on a short skiing holiday.”

11. Beratung zur Berufswahl.Diary March 11: “Albersheim asks my advice concerning choice of profession! He would like to stay in Vienna, conducting, teaching, or working for the Archive! He says that Hupka's position is almost hopeless: he is unable to gain any position. That reminds me of Hupka's naively stupid remark, when he once spent an evening with us: that my work was ‘hopeless’!”
15. Bach zweistimmige Invention Cdur, Bild korrigirt.

18. Bemerkungen zu Furtwänglers Vortrag der Jupiter-Sinfonie, in Handschrift u. Partitur verglichen.The program of the Vienna Philharmonic’s seventh subscription concert of the 1928/29 season comprised the “Jupiter” Symphony, Ernst Bloch’s Shelomo for cello and orchestra, and Brahms’s Fourth Symphony. A facsimile edition of the symphony was published by Universal Edition, Vienna, in 1923.
5. IV. In Köln.

8. Gespräch; Verlobung, Pläne;Diary April 8: “Albersheim [...] mentions his engagement to Miss Halden. He says that they will rent a small apartment, that they both want to teach; he would very much welcome the founding of a publishing house by Hoboken at which he might find a position.” zeigt den Versuch einer Darstellung der Jupiter-Sinfonie.

15. Zu Furtwänglers Vortrag der IX. Sinfonie.This note, also repeated in Angi Elias’s lesson notes, may refer to a recollection of a performance of the Ninth Symphony by Furtwängler, or to the composer’s remarks about his approach to the work. He is not known to have performed the work in early 1929.

19. Zeige die Antwort der Baronesse FischerDiary April 15: “From Albersheim (express postcard): he asks for the address of Baroness Fischer. — To him, the address. — To Baroness Fischer (express letter): I say that Albersheim will be in touch.” — Diary April 26: “To Baroness Fischer (letter): Albersheim will delay the examination, because he – does not need it!”
u. Weisse; er weicht einer Prüfung noch aus.
22. Bild der Fuge aus Händel Suite.
29. Abschluß der Fugen-Korrektur; Chopin Prélude, Bild korrigirt.
3. V. Schumann Etude symphonique Fragen.

6. Mozart Sinfonie abgeschlossen; Händel Suite II: Diminution im 2. Adagio; über den Unterschied von Händel u. Bach; über die Neigung Mozarts zu Dehnungen bei Gelegenheit von 3–3, bei IV7/3–V; Neigung zu Mischungen; Neigung zu Rhetorik bei Haydn; S. Bach vergleiche ich seiner Eindringlichkeit wegen mit der Therese von KonnersreuthTherese Naumann (1898–1962), German mystic who was born and spent her entire life in the Bavarian village of Konnersreuth. Her claims to have been cured of blindness and appendicitis by fervent prayer, and to have received the stigmata (the wounds that Christ suffered before his death) every Friday, made her a sensational figure in the 1920s. – auch Bach empfand alle Male Christi an sich, anders als Händel, der ganz in der Welt aufging; Bach: Gründer u. Zusammenhalter einer Familie, er begräbt Kinder, nimmt an Leichenbegängnissen anderer Teil als Kantor, in allen Prüfungen ganz Händel entgegengesetzt. Dieser, Opern-Unterneh-
-mer, macht Geschäftsreisen, feiert Helden, nicht Christus in Passionen, macht einige Konkurse durch, geht in einen Badeort! – Mozart Trio GdurOf Mozart’s two G major piano trios, K. 496 has a finale in the form of theme and variations, with coda.: eine klavier-technisch schwierige Stelle im Andante; Trio Gd letzter Satz: über die Variation Gmoll u. den Schluß, s. bei Brahms Schluß des Gdur Quintetts.

10. V. Brahms Rhapsodie Hm, neu.Diary May 5: “Fair copy of Brahms's Rhapsody in B minor (for Albersheim and Brünauer).” – Undated notes and a sketch for a graph of this work for Brünauer are preserved at OC 38/73 and other materials elsewhere in OC.
13. Fragen zu Tw. IV., Beispiele aus Händel, Mozart, Beethoven: ob oder ?Diary May 23: “I [answer] questions about the Tonwille 4 from Albersheim.”

24. Brahms op. 118 119 III Cdur, Linie korrigirt; zu Toscaninis Vortrag der Luzia; über die Unmöglichkeit Donizetti zu retten wegen seines Basses, der keine kontrapunktischen Prolongationen aufweist, vgl. Gluck, überhaupt die italienische u. französische Oper – oder den Jazz von heute. Nun ist aber die Musik im Abendland seit langem ein kontrapunktischer Satz bei dem auch der Baß wie eine Oberstimme
sich beträgt. Die abendländische Musik wird keine Erneuerung erfahren, bis sie nicht wieder zum Merkmal ihrer Geburt u. Frühzeit zurückkehrt, zum kontrapunktisch gehaltenen Außensatz. Ueber dem Unterschied von Rhythmik u. Metrik; über den Unterschied von „Technik“ u. wirklicher Technik. A. überrascht mich mit der Frage nach dem Gesetz vom Kopfton eines Zuges (!!)
27. Schnellfeuer von Fragen: aus der Instrumenten-Tabelle, über legato u. non legato bei Händel.

31. Ueberbringt einen Gruß von Rosé „mit besonderer Hochachtung“, ich sei mit dem älteren Bruder befreundet gewesen!Diary May 31: “Albersheim brings me greetings from Arnold Rosé, greetings of special esteem; he says that I had become a friend of his elder brother.” – Schenker himself confirms that he was “very good friends” with Alexander Rosé. Ueber den Unterschied von klassich u. romantisch in Musik, Malerei u. Architektur. Spielt die Händel-Fuge Fdur recht gut vor – ich korrigire Vortragsbemerkungen. Brahms–Haydn-Variationen, neu.Diary May 3: “From 2 to 4, I work on Brahms's Variations for Orchestra, as far as Variation 4 (for Albersheim).”

3. VI. Zur Methodik des Vor-
-trags; Erläuterung der Vortragsbezeichnung bei Brahms in der Sinfonie.Diary June 2: “I work for Albersheim.”
7. Chopin Sonate Fmoll Bmoll ,Diary June 4: “Fair copy of Chopin, Sonata in B minor, finale (Albersheim).” Finale, Bild korrigirt; über Zigeunermusik.
10. Fragen aus Chopin Polonaise, Prélude Fdur Bild korrigirt, Prélude Dm Bild korrigirt.
14. Fortsetzung u. Schluß der Brahms–Haydn Variationen.

21. Stellt in der letzten Stunde seine Braut vor – ich stelle ihm ein Zeugnis aus.Date supplied editorially on the basis of Schenker’s diary for June 21: “I attempt to get Albersheim to introduce his fiancée not after 1 o'clock, but actually earlier!”

tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Gerhard Albersheim in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: October 1: Mozart Eine kleine Nachtmusik; “Eroica” Symphony begun.
October 8: Mikulicz’s facsimile edition shown to him; the Minuet from Beethoven’s Op. 10, No. 3: passage with voice-exchange.
October 10: From Nottebohm’s sketchbook, sketches for the first movement, and how they are to be read.
October 19: First movement, correction of the graph completed.
October 22: Additional elucidations; entries from the revised copy of the score; performance, in broad outline.
October 26: Overture to A Midsummer Night’s Dream: graph of the Urlinie, unveiling of the deepest secrets of the parallelisms. Albersheim describes his visit to Nilius’s courses as a waste of time.
October 29: Second movement of the “Eroica” begun.
November 5: Further examination of the first movement, elucidation of several places in addition.

November 9: March from the music for A Midsummer Night’s Dream, graph of the Urlinie, and performance.
Observations on Hoesslins performance of Brahms’s First Symphony and Berlioz’s Symphonie fantastique; Scherzo begun.
November 16: Graph of the fourth movement. Questions about Schubert’s Symphony in B major.
November 26: Questions about Schubert’s Rosamunde ballet music, the passages in B major and G minor; I show him Heck’s sketches for Beethoven’s Sixth Symphony, last movement.
November 30: Voice-leading line for Schubert’s C major Symphony, the passage in F major in the Andante; line for Chopin’s Nocturne in F major corrected; line for Bach’s Toccata in F major corrected.

December 3: Mendelssohn “Die Liebende schreibt,” voice-leading line corrected; all manner of examples on performance: Mozart Rondo in A minor, Schubert Sonata in B major; I show the how far the Peters edition diverges from the facsimile of the autograph manuscript of Schubert’s Minuet in B minor.
December 7: Corrections to the graph of the finale completed, back to the Scherzo.
December 17: I show him Dunn’s Ornamentation and the reprint of Souchay; Chopin Etude Op. 10, No. 3, voice-leading line corrected.

December 21: Entries
made in the revised copy of the second, third and fourth movements completed; I recommend the article by Landshoff in Die Musik and Schoenberg’s interview with himself in the Deutsche Allgemeine Zeitung.
December 24: Performance of the second and third movements of the Symphony.
December 31: Performance of the finale; remarks on the performance of Beethoven’s Second Symphony (in contrast to Spörr on December 30).

January 4: Questions about ornamentation in Haydn’s sonatas, especially the turn figure from below; on the contradiction in the notation of in Schubert’s Symphony in B major, first movement; Haydn’s Symphony in D major begun.
January 7: Facsimile of Chopin’s Etude Op. 10, No. 12 shown to him; on the performance of Beethoven’s Piano Concerto in C major (by Wang).
January 11: Suggestions about Brahms’s Sonata for Violin and Piano, Op. 78, for a birthday celebration in Cologne.
January 21: I play the first movement of Handel’s Suite No. 2 and the Adagio from Beethoven’s Op. 13, etc.
January 25: Haydn, completion of the first movement, performance.
January 28: Studies in pedaling; I discuss Vrieslander’s corrections to Chopin’s Etude; Ornamentation in Haydn’s Sonata in E major in the editions of Moscheles and Päsler.
February 1: Haydn: the graph of the Andante.
February 4: Haydn: the graph of the Minuet.
February 8: I show him Hoboken’s march and Brünauer’s piano piece.
February 11: Haydn: finale. He is going on holiday until March 1.
March 4: Haydn completed, inclusive of performance.
March 8: Mozart’s Symphony in E major begun.
March 11: Advice on choice of profession.
March 15: Bach’s Invention in C major: the graph corrected.
March 18: Observations on Furtwängler’s performance of the “Jupiter” Symphony, the manuscript compared with the score.
April 5: He is in Cologne.
April 8: Conversation; engagement, plans; he shows me an attempt at a presentation of the “Jupiter” Symphony.
April 15: On Furtwängler’s performance of the Ninth Symphony.

April 19: I show him Baroness Fischer’s reply,
and Weisse’s; he is still avoiding an examination.
April 22: Graph of the fugue from Handel’s Suite.
April 29: Completion of the corrections to the fugue; Chopin Prelude, the graph corrected.
May 3: Questions about Schumann’s Symphonic Etudes.

May 6: Mozart’s symphony completed; Handel’s Suite No. 2: diminution in the second Adagio movement. On the difference between Handel and Bach. On Mozart’s penchant for expansions using 3–3, bei IV7/3–V; his penchant for mixtures of major and minor. Haydn’s penchant for rhetorical expression. I compare J. S. Bach, on account of his intensity, with Therese von Konnersreuth – Bach, too, found Christ at his side at all times, unlike Handel, who succeeded entirely as a man of the world. Bach: who creates a family and keeps it together, who buries children, who as cantor takes part in the funeral services, entirely the opposite to Handel in all his trials. The latter, opera entrepreneur,
takes business trips, celebrates heroes – not Christ in settings of the Passion – takes part in some competitions, goes to a bathing resort! – Mozart Trio in G major: a technically difficult passage in the Andante; last movement of the G major trio: on the G minor variation and the coda, cf. the close of Brahms’s Quintet in G major.
May 10: Brahms Rhapsody in B minor, new.
May 13: Questions about Der Tonwille issue 4, examples from Handel, Mozart, Beethoven: or ?

May 24: Brahms Op. 118 119 , No. 3, in C major, the voice-leading line corrected; on Toscanini’s performance of Lucia di Lammermoor; on the impossibility of rescuing Donizetti on account of his bass lines, which present no contrapuntal prolongations: compare Gluck, Italian and French opera in general – and today’s jazz. But for a long time, Western music has been a contrapuntal construction in which the bass, too, behaves as if it were an upper voice.
Western music will never experience regeneration until it returns to the sign of its birth and early times, to a contrapuntal outer-voice structure. On the difference between rhythm and meter; on the difference between “technique” and true technique. Albersheim surprises me with his question about the law of the primary tone of a linear progression. (!!)
May 27: Barrage of questions: from the Instrumentation Table, concerning legato and non legato in Handel.

May 31:He brings me a greeting from Rosé “with particular esteem,” as I have been a friend of his elder brother! On the difference between Classical and Romantic in music, painting, and architecture. He performs Handel’s fugue in F major very well – I correct the performance markings. Brahms’s Haydn Variations, new.
June 7: Chopin Sonata in F minor B minor , finale, graph corrected; on gypsy music.
June 10: Questions about a polonaise by Chopin; the graph of his Prelude in F major corrected, the graph of his Prelude in D minor corrected.
June 14: Continuation and conclusion of the Brahms Haydn Variations.
June 21: In the last lesson, he introduces me to his fiancée – I write a letter of reference for him.

tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Robert Brünauer in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: 1. X. Zeige ihm mein Urlinie-Blatt zur Chopin Etude op. 10I, Brahms op. 76III, Linie mündlich durchgegangen, erster Versuch zu spielen.Diary Oct 1: “Dr. Brünauer brings two first editions; perhaps they will be useful to Hoboken [...].”
4. Das Bild zuhause nachgeschrieben u. gezeigt.

8. Das Bild korrigirt.Diary Oct 8: “I show Beethoven's sketchbook [Landsberg 7] to Dr. Brünauer, he expresses great curiosity in it but complains: ‘… but I cannot buy everything (as if he had ever bought anything!), I shall make a point of looking at it, reading it and putting it back.’”
11. Gespielt.
15. Neues Bild zu Brahms, zum erstenmal in gepflegter Form! Ich trage den Hintergrund ein; gespielt.

18. Brahms 76VI
neu vorbereitet die Linie; Chopin Etude 10I: wederholt die Linie auf dem Klavier mit vorbildlicher Flüssigkeit. op. 10II: ich zeige die Linie, er wird sie aufschreiben.
22. Er bringt Brahms op. 76VI, eigene Linie, Vordergrund sogar mit Tinte geschrieben, bedeutender Fortschritt.

25. Nun auch den Hinter- u. Mittelgrund in das Blatt eingetragen, recht gut.Graphs of Brahms, Intermezzo in A major, Op. 76, No. 6 (see lesson note for October 22). Ich zeige zur Belohnung die Geheimnis wort se der Sommernachtstraum-Ouverture.
29. Chopin Etude 10II: Linie nachgeschrieben; ich zeige über Wunsch die Linie zu Chopin Prélude 1 u. 2.
5. XI. Ueber Beethovens Klavier-Violin-Sonate.There is a small gap at the end of this entry, suggesting that the key or opus number of the sonata was to be filled in later.

8. Bild zur Sinfonie Hm von Schubert aus Anlaß Berrsche.Alexander Berrsche, Ein Gespräch zum Schubert-Gedenktag, Der Kunstwart (November 1928); a fragment of this article is found in the Schenker Scrapbook (OC 2/page 76). Brahms op. 117I u. II wiederholt u. Chopin Nocturne Fisdur.

15. Bringt das Bild vom Prélude
Desdur, in der Hauptsache gelungen.Diary Nov 14: “I work on Chopin's Prelude in D major (for Brünauer).”

19. Im Bild des Prélude Desdur die Nebennote in 4 Stimmen durchgeführt;Diary Nov 18: “Prelude in D major (for Brünauer), the fair copy nearly completed.” – Diary Nov 21: I work on Beethoven's Op. 26 (for Brünauer).” ich zeige die Linie der Etude op. 25V, Gism.
22. Wiederholt S. Bach: Partita Bdur, Präludium u. aus der Suite Edur die Allemande.

26. Zeige Skizzen zur VI. Sinfonie (Heck); zu Furtwänglers Vortrag von Schuberts Cdur-Sinfonie.Schubert centenary concert, November 24, 1928, in the great hall of the Musikverein Building, Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra under Wilhelm Furtwängler, program: “Zauberharfe” Overture; six minuets and trios; Entracte to Rosamunde; C major Symphony. – Schenker attended and recorded in his diary: “From 3 to 4:45, concert: Furtwängler conducts the Philharmonic in a Schubert concert: Overture to Rosamunde and Five Minuets and Six Trios. In many of these short pieces, Furtwängler is quite excellent. To end with, the great Symphony in C major. He extends the character of the first movement to Beethovenian proportions, whereby the basic mood – the Schubertian humor – was lost. In the Andante, clarity in contrast was clearly lacking. Many things were also wanting in the last two movements; but it is to Furtwängler's credit that he possesses a very secure technique.” Im Prélude Desd die Ornamente genau analysiert, dann gespielt.

29. Bringt aus Eigenem das Bild des Schubert Menuetts Hm.This piece, the third movement of a piano sonata, forms the principal case study in Schenker’s Eine Rettung der klassischen Musik-Texte: Das Archiv für Photogramme in der National-Bibliothek, Wien (Widmung Anthony van Hoboken), in Der Kunstwart, 42/6 (March 1929), pp. 359–67.
6. XII. Zeige die eigene Darstellung der Nebennote im Prélude Desdur.
13. Chopin Etude op. 10II, Linie Stimmführung u. Spiel neu.
17. Bringt den Versuch der Linie von op. 10III, mißlungen!Diary Dec 15: “[I work on] Chopin's Op. 10, No. 3, for Brünauer.”

24. Gehe in der Stunde das Nebennotenbild aus dem Prélude Desd mit
ihm durch. Vortrag von op. 10III, neu.

27. Eine Stelle aus Beethoven op. 2III, (Damerow); zu Lach’s Festrede.Diary Dec 27: “From Miss Damerow (letter): question about Op. 2, No. 3, last movement.” – “From Rothberger (letter): Prof. Lach's speech.”
31. Vierhändig Mozart Sinfonie Ddur mit dem Oktavensprung zu Beginn u. Brahms Serenade Adur.
3. I. Händel Suite Fdur, neu; ich zeige die Linie in der Einleitung.
10. Korrektur des Bildes zu Händel begonnen.
14. Händel Triller, Fingersatz, Spiel.
21. Bringt das Bild zum Allegro ohne den ersten Satz vollendet zu haben! Ich spiele beide Sätze vor, lasse ihm nachspielen.

24. Bringt den a1-Teil einer dreiteiligen eigenen Komposition!Diary Jan 29: “I show [Hoboken] Brünauer's composition; he replies: ‘I too have a march, for piano four hands.’ I shall invite him to a first performance, his wife included.”
28. Bringt den mittleren Teil.
31. Gebe Winke zur Verfeinerung des Stückes; Korrektur des Allegro-Bildes begonnen.

4. II. Korrektur seiner Komposition fortgesetztDiary Feb 6: “Correction of Hoboken's and Brünauer's compositions.”; bringt ein neues
reineres Bild.

11. Ueberrascht mich mit den ersten 8 Takten eines neuen Stückes! Nun werde ich offener u. deutlicher über den praktischen Wert solcher Kompositionsübungen. Das Beste sei, daß dann Brünauer lerne von Brünauer! Eigentlich seien die Korrekturen im Stück schon enthalten, begreiflich bleiben die Töne gerade dem Verfasser noch stumm.
14. Das Bild der Diminutionen abgeschlossen.
18. Genauer Fingersatz zur Einleitung; Möglichkeiten des neuen Stückes erwogen.
21. Allegro; eine besondere Studie über die Auskomponierung vom V8–7.

25. Pläne zur neuen Komposition noch
einmal erwogen.Diary Feb 25: “I work on Brünauer's composition.”
7. III. Endlich ein schönes Bild vom Allegro, beide Teile.
11. Er möchte Tonwille-Hefte nachkaufen, die ihm fehlen!!Diary March 11: “Brünauer now wants to make the belated purchase nachkaufen of the issues of Der Tonwille !!” Werden wir fertig mit Händel?

Zu Casals Vortrag der Brahms Cello-Sonate op. 99;The concert took place on March 11, 1929 in the large hall of the Vienna Konzerthaus, Pablo Casals with Otto Schulhof, piano, program: Brahms, Cello Sonata in F major; Bach Cello Suite in D minor; Fauré, Sicilienne; Rimsky-Korsakov, Vol du Bourdon; Cassado, Folies; Saint-Saens, Appassionata; Locatelli, Sonata. – Schenker attended and recorded in his diary: “March 12, 1929: Casals concert: in every respect a beautiful program; he plays Brahms's Sonata in F major: the first two movements were less convincing, however the third and fourth movements proceeded with absolute perfection; Bach's Suite in D minor was equally convincing, the details as ever outstanding.” ich stelle ihn vor das Rätsel der Durchführung u. lüfte es schließlich worauf er: „Ich hätte es auch nicht anders gespielt“ – (!)

18. Zu Furtwänglers Vortrag der Jupiter-Sinfonie u. Brahms IV.The seventh Philharmonic subscription concert, in the great hall of the Musikverein Building on March 17, 1929, the Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra under Wilhelm Furtwängler. Schenker attended and recorded in his diary: “At 11 o'clock, walked to the concert. Conversation with Weisse, he says of Furtwängler: ‘and yet only a performer concerned with the foreground and effects.’ The first movement of the ‘Jupiter’ Symphony was pale; other shortcomings arise from insufficient knowledge of the score, especially in the Andante. A piece by Ernst Bloch – apparently a Zionist who, however, writes bad music. In Brahms's Fourth Symphony, much that is attractive – most of it, however, was unsatisfactory.”
25. Fingersatz u. Vortrag zum Allegro.
28. Chopin op. 10IV neu, zeige die Linie; Wiederholungen aus Händel Suite u. S. Bachs Suiten.
4. IV. Bringt das Händel Allegro auswendig geschrieben, recht gut. Wir machen in der Stunde das Bild vom 1. Teil der Etude.

Blattes.

15. Die Wiederholung von Brahms Rhapsodie Hmoll, 1. Teil wieder aufgenommen.

29. Fehlt wegen Grippe.

2. V. Skizziere die Linie der Rhapsodie selbst;Diary May 5: “Fair copy of Brahms's Rhapsody in B minor (for Albersheim and Brünauer)”. über das angeblich neue Thema in der Durchführung im 1. Satz der Eroica, hiezu Halm.August Halm, Der Fremdkörper im ersten Satz der Eroika, Die Musik 21 (1928–29), 481-84.

Br’s. | Sämann | diagram Lagenwechsel.“ – OC 38/73 is among a group of documents wrapped in a leaf from the magazine Radio Wien for February 1, 1929.

S. Bach; ich zeige den Hintergrund in der Rhapsodie; wiederholt die Berseuce.
13. Bringt das ausgebesserte Bild der Rhapsodie u. spielt das Stück. Zum Schluß der Stunde: „Ich möchte spielen“ (!) „auch einzelne Stellen“ (!!) Ich tröste ihn.

16. „Spiele ich nicht schlechter?“Diary May 16: “Brünauer: ‘I am playing worse’; as the result of a lost lesson, a forced word!” „10–12 Stücke möchte ich gern spielen können.“ Nun setze ich ihm den Unterschied der Disziplinen auseinander: Schneller lauft das Schreiben der Stimmführung ab, einmal geschrieben ist für immer geschrieben, dagegen fordert das Klavierspiel ständige Pflege wie z.B. der Körper – was ihm ja aber nicht liegt – wo ist da ein Ausweg?

„wäre mir spielen u. das Andere nur so.“ (!) Also ein Rückfall ins frühere Durcheinander ohne Grundlage.Diary May 23: “Brünauer: ‘That is how I like it: playing, enlivened with voice-leading.’ He plays, I accompany his playing with voice-leading and theory (using my work with Miss Kahn as a model). I remark: For voice-leading one needs a writing implement; for playing, practice.”
27. Er zeigt eine Fortsetzung der eigenen Komposition.

tei:div.tei:note: The lesson reports for Robert Brünauer in the original are written continuously, without paragraph breaks or separating punctuation. They have been separated here in the interests of legibility.
tei:div.tei:ab: October 1: I show him my Urlinie graph of Chopin’s Etude Op. 10, No. 1. Brahms Op. 76, No. 3, the voice-leading line gone through orally; his first attempt at playing it
October 4: The graph written out at home and shown to me
October 8: The graph corrected.
October 11: Played.
October 15: New graph for Brahms, for the first time in proper form! I enter the background; the work is played.

October 18: Brahms Op. 76, No. 6,
the voice-leading line newly prepared; Chopin Etude Op. 10, No. 1: the line repeated at the piano with exemplary fluency. Op. 10, No. 2: I show him the line, he will write it down.
October 22: He brings his own voice-leading line for Brahms Op. 76, No. 6, the foreground even written in ink; significant progress.
October 25: Now the background and middleground entered on the page, very good. As a reward, I show him the secrets of the Overture to A Midsummer Night’s Dream.
October 29: Chopin Etude Op. 10, No. 2: the voice-leading line copy; at his request, I show him the lines for Chopin’s Preludes No. 1 and No. 2.
November 5: Concerning Beethoven’s Sonata for Violin and Piano.
November 8: Graph of Schubert’s Symphony in B minor, on the occasion of Berrsche. Brahms Op. 117, No. 1 and No. 2, revisited, and Chopin Nocturne in F major.

November 15: He brings the graph of the Prelude
in D major, successful in the main points.
November 19: In the graph of the Prelude in D major, the neighbor-note realized in four-voice harmony; I show him the voice-leading line of the Etude in G minor, Op. 25, No. 5.
November 22: The Prelude from J. S. Bach’s Partita in B major, and the Allemande from the French Suite in E major.

November 26: I show him sketches for the Sixth Symphony (Heck); on Furtwängler’s performance of Schubert’s Symphony in C major. In the Prelude in D major, the ornaments analyzed precisely, then played.
November 29: He brings on his own initiative the graph of Schubert’s Minuet in B minor.
December 6: I show him my representation of the neighbor-note in the Prelude in D major.
December 13: Chopin Etude Op. 10, No. 2: line, voice-leading, and playing.
December 17: He brings an attempt at the voice-leading line for Op. 10, No. 3: unsuccessful!

December 24: In the lesson, I go through the graphic representation of the neighbor-note in the Prelude in D major.
Performance of Op. 10, No. 3, new.
December 27: A passage from Beethoven’s Op. 2, No. 3 (Damerow); on Lach’s festival speech.
December 31: Mozart’s Symphony in D major (which begins with the octave leap) and Brahms’s Serenade in A major played four-hands.
January 3: Handel Suite in F major, new; I show him the voice-leading line in the introduction.
January 10: Correction of the graph for Handel begun.
January 14: Handel: trills, fingering, playing.
January 21: He brings the graph for the Allegro without having finished the first movement! I play both movements to him and have him play after me.
January 24: He brings the a1 section of a three-part composition of his own!
January 28: He brings the middle section of a composition of his own.
January 31: I offer hints on the refinement of the piece that he has composed; correction of the graph of the Allegro begun.

February 4: Corrections to his composition continued; he brings a new,
cleaner graph.
February 7: I show him my corrections to his composition. Particular study of diminutions in the introduction to the Handel.

February 11: He surprises me with the first eight bars of a new piece. Now I shall be more open, and clearer, about the practical value of such compositional exercises. The best is that Brünauer is learning from Brünauer! In fact, the corrections are already contained in the piece; understandably, the notes still remain silent to the composer himself.
February 14: The graph of the diminutions completed.
February 18: A precise fingering for the introduction possibilities for the new piece considered.
February 21: Allegro; a particular study of the composing-out of V8–7.

February 25: Plans for the new composition
considered once again.
March 7: Finally a beautiful graph of the Allegro, both sections.
March 11: He would like to buy the issues of Der Tonwille that he is missing!! Have we finished with Handel?

March 14: On Casals’ performance of Brahms’s Cello Sonata Op. 99; I present him with the puzzle of the development section and clarify it for him in the end, upon which he says: “I too would not have played it differently” – (!)
March 18: On Furtwängler’s performance of the “Jupiter” Symphony and Brahms’s Fourth Symphony.
March 25: Fingering and performance of the Allegro.
March 28: Chopin Op. 10, No. 4, new; I show him the voice-leading line. Revisitations from Handel’s Suite and J. S. Bach’s suites.
April 4: He brings the Handel Allegro written out from memory, very good. During the lesson we make the graph of the first part of the Etude.

April 8: Thorough correction of the
sheet written out from memory.
April 11: Brünauer plays the Etude in C minor.
April 15: Revisitation of Brahms’s Rhapsody in B minor; the first part taken up again.
April 18: Handel, third movement, new graph.
April 22: He writes out the Fugue in four-voice open score; he returns once more to the diminutions in the Adagio.
April 25: Sketch of the voice-leading line for the Rhapsody.
April 29: He is absent, on account of the flu.
May 2: I sketch the voice-leading line of the Rhapsody myself. On the supposedly new theme in the development section of the first movement of the “Eroica”; with regard to this, Halm.

May 6: The results of contemplating the Rhapsody lead to a characteristic of Brahms; like a sower, he disseminates arpeggiations and changes of register: diagram: 6 lines diverging from left point. Haydn’s Andante in F minor, the voice-leading line of the theme.

May 9: (in place of June 27): on the performance of J. S. Bach’s Chaconne for solo violin;
I show him the background of the Rhapsody; he repeats the Berceuse.
May 13: He brings the improved graph of the Rhapsody and plays the piece. At the end of the lesson: “I would like to play” (!) “individual passages, too” (!!) I comfort him.

May 16:“Am I not playing any worse?" “I would like to be able to play ten or twelve pieces.” Now I explain to him the difference between the disciplines. Writing out the voice-leading proceeds more quickly: once written, it is written forever. By contrast, piano playing requires constant attention as, for example, is required by the body – which is something that is not in his nature – how can one get around this?

May 23: He revisits Brahms’s Waltzes No. 1, No. 2, and No. 3. “I would like best of all to play,
the other stuff only as a pretence.” (!) Thus a regression to the earlier jumble, without foundation.
May 27:He shows me a continuation of his own composition.
June 3: Brahms’s Capriccio from Op. 76 revisited.
June 6: Brahms’s Waltz No. 4 revisited.
June 17: I show him how one should practice, using examples: Chopin’s Etude Op. 10, No. 5, in G major, etc.

Zu Furtwänglers Vortrag der Schubert Sinfonie Cd;Schubert centenary concert, November 24, 1928, in the great hall of the Musikverein Building, Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra under Wilhelm Furtwängler, program: “Zauberharfe” Overture; six minuets and trios; Entracte to Rosamunde; C major Symphony. – Schenker attended and recorded in his diary: “From 3 to 4:45, concert: Furtwängler conducts the Philharmonic in a Schubert concert: Overture to “Rosamunde” and Five Minuets and Six Trios. In many of these short pieces, Furtwängler is quite excellent. To end with, the great Symphony in C major. He extends the character of the first movement to Beethovenian proportions, whereby the basic mood – the Schubertian humor – was lost. In the Andante, clarity in contrast was clearly lacking. Many things were also wanting in the last two movements; but it is to Furtwängler's credit that he possesses a very secure technique.” über die Ornamente im Prélude Desd; Bindung durch Steigerung (vgl.
